sources.title: Quandela demonstrates its GPU–QPU integration architecture using NVIDIA NVQLink
sources.boundary: The GTC Berlin demonstrator's QPU is simulated; the post separately refers to earlier physical-QPU integration validation without a complete independently audited cost/latency ledger.

sources.title: Quandela and Quanova partner to deploy Vietnam’s first quantum computer
sources.boundary: Planned deployment and education/research program; no verified operational endpoint, UQPU access, or price.

lanes.A: QEC decoder latency and accepted logical operation become explicit workload-level metrics; no quantum advantage claimed.
lanes.B: Provider surveillance updated; no new adapter or access claim.
lanes.C: Syndrome payload, host/controller/GPU transfers, buffering and reconstruction must be counted.
lanes.D: Photonic QPU/controller interface co-design remains downstream of measured latency and control requirements.
lanes.E: No direct biomass, bio-oil, fusion or energy result.
lanes.F: Total cost must include classical decoder, accelerator, host, network, retries and provider charges.
lanes.G: Manufacturing/packaging questions identified, no yield or equipment result.
lanes.H: Regional provider development recorded as market context, not scientific or commercial proof.

next_gate: Pin and independently reproduce the simulated AWS Ising Decoding workload, then measure full per-round latency and cost at a frozen logical-error target; separately verify any photonic provider endpoint, modality, API, pricing and authorization.
evidence_boundary: No UQPU advantage, new physical law, material substitution, accepted fuel, net fusion electricity, financing benefit or Data-Center-to-One-Phone result is established.
